text_blocks.snippet: Common scams in Central Illinois include fake traffic/toll violation text messages, utility "slamming" switches, and sweepstakes or prize notifications.

list.snippet: Fake Traffic & Toll Texts: Scammers send text messages pretending to be from the state or toll agencies, claiming you owe fines for unpaid tickets or tolls and threatening license suspensions.
Utility Slamming: Con artists pose as local energy or utility providers (like Homefield Energy or Ameren Choice) trying to trick you into switching your electricity supplier.
Package Delivery Smishing: Fraudulent texts claim a package delivery is delayed or missing an address, prompting you to click a link and input credit card or personal info.
Sweepstakes and Prizes: Calls or messages claiming you have won millions of dollars, but requiring an upfront fee or personal bank details to claim it.
Government/Imposter Scams: Scammers spoof phone numbers to impersonate local police, the IRS, or the Social Security Administration, demanding immediate payment via gift cards or peer-to-peer apps.
Do not click links: Never click on links in unsolicited text messages or emails regarding tolls, packages, or traffic fines.
Verify independently: Government agencies and utility companies will not text or call demanding immediate payment or personal data. Look up official numbers independently to verify.

Report fraud: If you receive suspicious messages, report them to the Illinois Attorney General

or check local advisories via the Better Business Bureau of Central Illinois.
